name: Workday
summary: Workday has no central OAuth app the developer can register: each customer's Workday tenant admin must run the 'Register API Client' task inside their own tenant (producing a per-tenant client ID/secret) and hand over tenant-specific authorize/token endpoints, so the developer cannot self-serve production access.
difficultyWhy: OAuth clients live inside each customer tenant and are created by that customer's Workday administrator, so the developer depends on every customer and cannot obtain one global client ID/secret. A free developer tenant exists for building and testing, but production reach needs customer admins (and optionally partner/marketplace approval).

time.setup: ~15-30 min per tenant for an admin who has the security permissions (developer sandbox tenant: ~15 min to provision)
time.approval: No central OAuth approval; each customer's internal change/security review (days to weeks, unverified). Built on Workday app review and Partner Order timing unpublished.
time.total: Developer sandbox: same day. Each production customer: days to weeks depending on the customer's admin and change process (inferred). Marketplace/partner route: unknown, likely weeks to months.

devModeLimits: A free personal-account development tenant on the Workday Build / Open Developer Platform lets you register your own API client against that sandbox only. Limits: one active development tenant at a time, max two created per 6 hours, tenant expires after 7 consecutive days without login. It holds no real customer data and cannot connect to customer tenants.

stages.duration: ~15 min after creating a free Workday Build account

steps.title: Decide which Workday model you are on
steps.detail: Workday has no public app console where a third party registers one OAuth app that works for all customers. The API client is registered inside each customer tenant ('Register API Client' task), so client ID/secret are per-tenant. Alternatives: (a) per-customer API client (what Composio custom auth supports), (b) become a Workday partner and ship a 'Built on Workday' / Extend app that customers install from their App Manager, or (c) use ISU credentials or a refresh token generated by the customer admin.

steps.title: Get a developer sandbox tenant (for building and testing only)
steps.detail: Create a free account on the Workday Build platform with a personal email at developer.workday.com. Open Console > Tenants, click the + under Development Tenants and submit a request. Workday emails you (about 15 minutes per the docs) with sign-in details; sign in as lmcneil and change the password within 72 hours. One active tenant at a time; it expires after 7 days without login. A Workday blog post (27 Aug 2026) describes 'pilot access' via a waitlist at developer.workday.com/about; the getting-started doc describes self-serve creation, so current status of the waitlist is unclear.

steps.title: Customer admin: enable required functional areas and security
steps.detail: A Workday tenant administrator with sufficient security permissions must make sure the Workday account that will authorize has access to the data via domain security policies, and run 'Activate Pending Security Policy Changes' after any policy change. Okta's guide shows the pattern of enabling functional areas in 'Maintain Functional Areas' and granting Get/Put on the relevant domains before registering the client. For ISU-based (non-interactive) access the admin also runs 'Create Integration System User' (Session Timeout Minutes = 0, exempt from password expiration), creates an Integration System Security Group, adds the ISU, and grants domain permissions via 'Maintain Permissions for Security Group'.

steps.title: Customer admin: run 'Register API Client' in the tenant
steps.detail: Search the tenant for 'Register API Client'. Client Name: unique descriptive name (e.g. 'Your App via Composio'). Client Grant Type: Authorization Code Grant. Access Token Type: Bearer. Redirection URI: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (Workday reportedly allows only one redirect URI per client). Tick 'Non-Expiring Refresh Tokens'. Scope (Functional Areas): choose the areas that secure the endpoints you will call, e.g. Staffing, HRIS, System, Tenant Non-Configurable, Personal Data, Time Off and Leave, Recruiting; optionally 'Include Workday Owned Scope'. Click OK. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret immediately: the secret is not shown again after leaving the screen.

steps.title: Collect tenant-specific endpoints
steps.detail: Admin runs the 'View API Clients' report and copies the Authorization Endpoint, Token Endpoint and Workday REST API Endpoint. Observed patterns: authorize = https://<authorization-domain>/<tenant>/authorize; token = https://<token-domain>/ccx/oauth2/<tenant>/token; REST = https://<host>/ccx/api/v1/<tenant>/<resource>. The authorization, token and REST hosts can differ, especially on implementation (IMPL) or sandbox tenants, so use exact values from the report. Tenant name is case-sensitive.

steps.title: Optional: generate a refresh token for an ISU (API Client for Integrations)
steps.detail: For server-to-server style access, the admin runs 'Register API Client for Integrations', then in 'View API Clients' > 'API Clients for Integrations' tab selects the client, API Client > 'Manage Refresh Tokens for Integrations', enters the ISU in the 'Workday Account' field, ticks the generate/regenerate option and saves the refresh token. The refresh token must be non-expiring or refresh can fail.

steps.title: Create a Composio custom auth config per customer tenant
steps.detail: In Composio create a custom OAuth2 auth config for the WORKDAY toolkit with that tenant's Client ID, Client Secret and endpoints. Composio's toolkit page confirms there is no managed OAuth for Workday. Because Workday credentials and endpoints are per tenant, expect one auth config per customer tenant, or a custom flow if Composio cannot template tenant host/name (unverified).

steps.title: Optional: partner / marketplace route
steps.detail: Workday offers Innovation Partner (Build), Sales and Services partner programmes via a partner portal. Apps built on the platform can be distributed as 'Built on Workday' apps: create the app on the Developer Site, submit for review from the Approval Status section, Workday approves, promote to Production, then complete the Partner Order process in the Built on Workday Digital Resource Room. Customers then install from App Manager. Requirements for the Partner Order and for Marketplace listing are not public.

requirements: For production: a customer with a Workday tenant and an administrator who has security access to run Register API Client, View API Clients and security policy tasks.
For sandbox: a free Workday Build / developer.workday.com account using a personal email (eligibility criteria not stated).
For the 'Built on Workday' distribution route: membership of a Producer account, Developer Site access, and a WCP development tenant account; then Workday review and the Partner Order process.
For partner status (Innovation Partner etc.): application via the Workday partner portal; criteria and fees not public.
Each customer's tenant must have OAuth 2.0 clients enabled (per Runlayer docs), and the registering admin or authorizing user needs domain security access to the data.
gotchas: Client ID/secret are per customer tenant: there is no single global OAuth app. One auth config per tenant is the likely shape.

Authorize URL contains the customer's Workday host and tenant name; token URL contains the data-center host and /ccx/oauth2/<tenant>/token. Hosts for authorize, token and REST can all differ, especially on IMPL/sandbox tenants.
Sources disagree on token URL shape: Nango shows /ccx/oauth2/<tenant>/token, Reco shows /ccx/oauth2/token. Copy exactly from the customer's View API Clients report.
The client secret is displayed only once on the registration confirmation screen.
Workday reportedly allows only one redirect URI per API client (CData docs), so the Composio callback must be entered exactly; a client cannot also serve other redirect URIs.
Tick 'Non-Expiring Refresh Tokens' at registration. Without a refresh token users must reauthenticate when the short-lived access token expires; a provided refresh token must be non-expiring.

Scopes are Workday functional areas, and their names vary by Workday release. Check the 'Secured by' section of each REST API in the tenant's own REST API reference. Missing domain permissions show up as 403.

Workday's own docs list https://cb.myworkday.com/cb1 (and cb-eu.myworkday.com/cb1) as the callback for Workday-as-client scenarios (Extend apps calling external OAuth providers); it is not the callback for this flow.
ISU access ignores the end user's own security, so an ISU can expose more data than the individual user should see. Customers' security teams may push back.
Sandbox/developer tenants are not customer tenants: working there proves the flow but gives no access to customer data. A developer tenant expires after 7 days of inactivity.
Workday also offers a separate Extend API gateway/auth (api.<region>.wcp.workday.com/auth); that is for Extend apps and not the customer-tenant OAuth endpoints used here.
Data-centre/region differences (US, EU, etc.) affect hosts; the Developer Site warns that using a gateway for the wrong region returns 401.

blockers.blocker: Customer admin cannot or will not register an API client
blockers.symptom: Customer has no admin with the required security permissions, or their security/change process rejects an external OAuth client.
blockers.whatToDo: Provide the customer a one-page admin checklist (grant type, redirect URI, functional areas, non-expiring refresh token, endpoints to send back) and a minimal-scope justification. Offer an ISU with a constrained security group as an alternative.
blockers.escalation: The customer's Workday administrator or their Workday implementation partner.

blockers.blocker: Cannot reach customers at scale without a Workday partnership
blockers.symptom: Every customer requires bespoke admin work; no marketplace presence to build trust.
blockers.whatToDo: Apply to the Workday partner programme (Innovation Partner) and evaluate distributing as a Built on Workday app; these processes are gated and criteria are not public.

blockers.blocker: Developer tenant not available or waitlisted
blockers.symptom: Cannot create a development tenant, or the Workday blog says to join a waitlist.
blockers.whatToDo: Check developer.workday.com Console > Tenants; if unavailable, join the waitlist or test against a friendly customer's sandbox/IMPL tenant.

blockers.blocker: Authorization or token calls fail against the tenant
blockers.symptom: Wrong host, 404 on /authorize or /token, invalid_client, or 403 on API calls.
blockers.whatToDo: Re-copy Authorization Endpoint, Token Endpoint and REST endpoint from the tenant's View API Clients report; confirm tenant name case; confirm the client's functional areas and the user's domain security, then run Activate Pending Security Policy Changes.

blockers.blocker: Composio custom auth config cannot express per-tenant authorize/token URLs
blockers.symptom: Auth config form only takes a client ID and secret, not tenant host and name.
blockers.whatToDo: Ask Composio support how Workday tenant host/tenant name are supplied; otherwise create one auth config per tenant or use a refresh-token/ISU-based approach.

agentCanDo: Draft the exact admin checklist (Register API Client field values, functional areas, redirect URI) to send to each customer's Workday admin.
Explain how to read the View API Clients report and derive authorize, token and REST URLs and the tenant name.
Validate pasted endpoint URLs and tenant name against the observed patterns.
Create the Composio custom auth config once the customer provides credentials (via the developer's Composio access).
Prepare a security justification for requested functional areas and draft partner-programme and customer outreach text.
youMustDo: Create the Workday Build account and request a development tenant (personal email, password setup within 72 hours).
Get each customer's Workday administrator to run Register API Client and security configuration in their tenant: the developer cannot do this for them.
Receive and store each customer's Client ID and Client Secret securely (the secret is shown once).
Apply to the Workday partner programme and complete Built on Workday review, Partner Order and legal agreements if going the marketplace route.
Handle any customer security review, contracts and data-processing terms.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Workday (confirmed on its toolkit page). The customer admin must enter the Composio callback as the single Redirection URI when running Register API Client. Because client credentials and authorize/token hosts are per tenant, plan one auth config per customer tenant; whether Composio's config can take a tenant host and tenant name is unverified.

evidence.claim: Composio-managed OAuth is not available for the Workday toolkit; you must supply your own OAuth2 credentials; page does not list scopes or tenant fields.

A Workday tenant administrator runs 'Register API Client' in the tenant with Grant Type Authorization Code Grant, Access Token Type Bearer, a Redirection URI, non-expiring refresh tokens checkbox and functional-area scopes; Client ID and Secret are generated.
evidence.note: Third-party vendor docs, not Workday's own login-gated docs.

evidence.claim: Okta's guide confirms the same registration (Authorization Code Grant, Bearer, non-expiring refresh tokens, functional areas) and that the client secret is permanently hidden after leaving the confirmation screen; the admin also runs Maintain Functional Areas and Activate Pending Security Policy Changes.

Authorization endpoint pattern https://<authorization-domain>/<tenant>/authorize and token endpoint pattern https://<token-domain>/ccx/oauth2/<tenant>/token; values come from the View API Clients report; REST base also uses the token domain.
evidence.note: Derived by Nango from example endpoints. Reco's article shows a different token path (/ccx/oauth2/token), so exact shape varies.

evidence.claim: REST URL format is https://{host}/ccx/api/v1/{tenant}/{resource}, e.g. host wd2-impl-services1.workday.com; token request uses Basic auth with refresh_token grant.

Authorization, token and REST hosts may differ especially on implementation or sandbox tenants; tenant name is case-sensitive; scope areas vary by Workday version, check each API's 'Secured by' section.
evidence.note: Runlayer uses PKCE as a public client; Workday's confidential-client option (client secret) is what Nango/Okta describe.

evidence.claim: Register API Client for Integrations plus 'Manage Refresh Tokens for Integrations' lets an admin bind an ISU and generate a refresh token; ISU needs Session Timeout 0, password-expiry exemption, security group and domain GET permissions.
evidence.note: Workato says the Register API Client for Integrations task is required only for custom objects in its use case.

evidence.claim: Workday allows only one redirect URI per application; Authorization Code and ISU/JWT variants exist.
evidence.note: Single vendor claim; not confirmed on a Workday doc.

evidence.claim: Free Workday Build developer account with personal email; development tenant created from Console > Tenants; provisioning described as 1-2 minutes in one doc and about 15 minutes in another.
evidence.note: Docs disagree on timing (1-2 min vs ~15 min).

evidence.claim: Personal account development tenant limits: one active tenant, no more than two in 6 hours, expires after 7 consecutive days without login; eligibility is Personal Account developers via the Open Developer Platform programme.
Workday announced pilot access to its Open Developer Platform with a waitlist at developer.workday.com/about, dated 27 Aug 2026; developers get their own Workday tenant.
evidence.note: The fetched developer.workday.com/about page did not mention a waitlist, so waitlist status is unclear.

evidence.claim: Workday partner programme types: Innovation Partners (Build), Sales Partners (Grow), Services Partners (Deliver); Workday Marketplace has solutions 'built on and certified for' the platform; requirements and process not listed publicly on that page.

Built on Workday app distribution: Producer account, developer site access, WCP dev tenant account; submit for review in the Approval Status section, Workday approves, promote to Production, complete Partner Order process; customers install from App Manager.
evidence.note: Approval criteria and Partner Order details not public.

evidence.claim: Extend ISU authentication: admin assigns ISU to an app in App Manager, which creates an API client; Company Administrator adds tenant consent when promoting to non-development tenants; ISU access can bypass end-user security.
evidence.note: Applies to Extend apps, not to the customer-tenant Register API Client flow.

evidence.claim: Workday tenant callback URLs for Workday-as-client scenarios are https://cb.myworkday.com/cb1 and https://cb-eu.myworkday.com/cb1; Extend gateways are api.<region>.wcp.workday.com with /auth for authorization.
evidence.note: Gateway info from https://developer.workday.com/doc/dlh1653340161856.md. Neither is used by the Composio customer-tenant flow.

evidence.claim: Each production customer must perform its own registration, so there is one client ID/secret per customer tenant and no global developer-owned OAuth app.
evidence.note: Inferred from the Register API Client task being run inside the tenant by its admin; no Workday doc read that states this outright.

evidence.claim: Lead time per customer is days to weeks, driven by the customer's admin availability and change/security review.
evidence.note: No source gives timings; this is an estimate.

evidence.claim: Composio needs one auth config per customer tenant, and may not be able to template tenant host/name in authorize/token URLs.
evidence.note: Composio's toolkit page does not describe tenant fields; confirm with Composio.

evidence.claim: Exact security domains and Workday-side permissions an admin needs to run Register API Client, and the official Workday doc for it.
evidence.note: doc.workday.com and Workday Community docs are login-gated and were not read.
